chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
He who gives with his short hand is given by a long hand.

key_terms.الْيَدِ الطَّوِيلَةِ: the long hand (metaphor for abundant divine reward)
key_terms.الْيَدِ الْقَصِيرَةِ: the short hand (metaphor for modest or small giving)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to give with a short hand versus a long hand in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of the 'short hand' to represent the limited capacity of the giver, contrasting it with God's 'long hand' of boundless generosity. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) and the divine principle that God multiplies the reward of modest charity far beyond its material value, encouraging believers not to withhold giving due to perceived insufficiency.
